claims.conditions: The agent is about to state that work is complete, fixed or passing, or to commit, push or open a pull request, and a command that can prove the claim exists and can be run in the session. Invocation must already be permitted by the user, the harness and applicable policy; this claim describes suitability under the stated conditions and grants no permission to invoke.
claims.rationale: The source's rule is 'NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE' (line 17): 'If you haven't run the verification command in this message, you cannot claim it passes' (line 20), followed by a five-step gate to identify the proving command, run it in full, read the output, verify, and only then claim (lines 25-31). A subagent's success report is to be checked against a version-control diff rather than accepted (line 47). The text contains no instruction to ask or wait for a person, and it needs no tool beyond the proving command, so it is a self-contained gate a model can apply to its own claims. Plausible failure modes: the text gives no path when the proving command cannot be run, so the agent may substitute a weaker command and still claim; a full fresh run before every status statement is costly on long suites; the regression-test check reverts and restores a fix (line 84), which an interruption can leave reverted. Falsified if a session that has loaded and read this text states that work passes or is complete in a message that contains no fresh run of a proving command.
